purpose: Natural documentary-style imagery for fictional concept projects; not photographs of commissioned client work.

prompts.prompt: Use case: product-mockup. Create an ORIGINAL fictional portfolio concept for a practical luggage business named 'NORTHBOUND TRAVEL'. Wide landscape image 1536x1024, genuinely ordinary commercial photography, understated and realistic, not a cinematic luxury render. A black 14-inch laptop sits open on a normal light oak desk in a small product design studio on an overcast day. Its screen shows a restrained, professionally designed luggage e-commerce homepage: small black uppercase NORTHBOUND TRAVEL wordmark, white navigation, clear headline 'Ready for the long way.', documentary photograph of a simple dark navy fabric carry-on, straightforward product categories. To the right of the laptop is that same navy soft-sided four-wheel carry-on with black handle and a simple white woven NORTHBOUND TRAVEL label, plus a folded paper product hangtag. Physical objects have credible dimensions and small everyday imperfections; slightly scuffed desk edge, realistic laptop reflections, tiny paper creases. Soft neutral window light, natural white balance, subdued contrast, normal office rather than an extravagant set. Eye-level three-quarter framing, tack-sharp readable brand name, honest commercial documentation of a design concept. No tan arches, terracotta walls, orange light, dramatic sun rays, floating objects, fake embossed metal, excessive depth of field, unrealistic product anatomy, awards, fake ratings, watermarks, Apple logos, stock-photo handshakes, or competing brands. Keep branding limited and typography exact.

Use case: product-mockup. Create an ORIGINAL fictional furniture business identity presentation for 'MASON & REED'. Wide landscape 1536x1024. It must resemble a straightforward photograph of real printed design work on an agency desk, not a 3D render or an AI luxury advertisement. Overhead camera on an ordinary pale grey studio table. A modest A4 furniture catalogue, a few small off-white business cards, a folded product specification sheet, and a simple black folder are laid out neatly but not with impossible symmetry. The catalogue cover has the perfectly spelled black wordmark 'MASON & REED', a small clear MR typographic monogram, and a natural photograph of a practical solid-oak chair with black upholstered seat. Small muted sage-green accents, uncoated white paper, ordinary black ink, light print grain, subtle paper curl, tiny alignment imperfections. Neutral soft side window light, accurate natural shadows, modest real-world print-production feel, believable paper thickness and furniture photograph. Text limited to MASON & REED and small 'Furniture for everyday living.' No gold foil, stone plinths, orange sunlight, arches, dramatic casting shadows, sculptural impossible chairs, leathery paper, flowers, design awards, fake addresses, watermarks or stock logos. Original fictional concept; do not use any real client identity.

Use case: ui-mockup. Generate a believable documentary photograph of original website design work for a fictional everyday homewares shop named 'FIELDWORK SUPPLY'. Wide landscape 1536x1024. A normal silver laptop, no visible manufacturer branding, on a slightly worn white studio desk, viewed nearly front-on from a mild elevated angle so the actual screen is readable and the screen design is the focus. Display a complete, precise, restrained e-commerce homepage: black small FIELDWORK SUPPLY wordmark top left, clean white navigation, heading 'Useful things. Well made.', a calm natural photograph of a plain white ceramic mug and folded navy cotton kitchen towel on a wooden counter, and below it a straightforward three-product grid of mug, cotton towel, and small storage tin. Off-white website, black typography, very limited navy accent; tidy professional layout, actual plausible UI spacing rather than a fantasy screen. A printed site wireframe and a graphite pencil beside the laptop, no other props. Neutral cloudy window daylight, natural camera exposure, realistic reflections, sensible physical scale, mild normal photographic grain. Not a glossy 3D mockup, no levitating screen, no terracotta, no artificial golden sunlight, no surreal sculptural products, no business claims, no fake testimonials or ratings, no watermarks or Apple branding. Only brand name and main headline need legibility; keep secondary copy quiet.

Use case: product-mockup. Original fictional architecture-practice branding sample for 'BRACKEN STUDIO'. Wide landscape 1536x1024, ordinary natural editorial photograph documenting a graphic designer's printed work. On an architect's white desk are a flat white presentation folder with a small black BRACKEN STUDIO wordmark and a simple bold B monogram, two matte white business cards with black typography and one fine muted green rule, a carefully folded A3 architectural floor plan with clean realistic technical lines, and a modest recycled-paper envelope carrying the same BRACKEN STUDIO name. Use case: ui-mockup. Produce a credible original software product design presentation for a fictional business tool called 'STOCKROOM'. Wide landscape 1536x1024, neutral documentary photograph of a real desktop workstation. A single normal black 24-inch monitor and plain compact keyboard on a practical light grey desk. On the monitor, show a meticulously designed, usable warehouse order-management web application: small STOCKROOM wordmark top left; narrow white sidebar with 'Overview', 'Orders', 'Inventory', 'Suppliers'; main heading 'Orders'; simple top-right 'New order' button; clean readable table with column labels 'Order', 'Customer', 'Status', 'Total'; four restrained rows using small neutral status labels 'Packed', 'Processing', 'Dispatched'. White UI, graphite type, modest navy highlights, generous legible spacing, small practical information summary without fake revenue metrics or performance claims. The screen occupies most of the photograph and looks like a genuine normal browser at 100% zoom, not a holographic futuristic dashboard. A few ordinary pencil annotations on paper beside the keyboard, realistic screen glare low enough to read, natural overcast daylight, no coloured lighting, no coding matrix screens. No dramatic cinematic colour grade, no fake sales charts, no glow, no floating devices, no marble or terracotta, no logos of hardware manufacturers, no watermark. No people. This is an illustrative product interface study.

Use case: product-mockup. Original fictional small coffee business brand and advertising concept called 'CORNERSTONE COFFEE'. Wide landscape 1536x1024. A realistic, modest commercial photograph of freshly printed coffee packaging: two practical brown kraft coffee pouches with correct folded gussets, one standing and one laid flat, simple white rectangular paper labels printed in dark charcoal with the exact name CORNERSTONE COFFEE and small words 'House blend'. All on an ordinary clean café counter of light grey laminate with a real stainless edge visible at one side. No fancy luxury scene, no styled foliage, no scattered beans everywhere. Neutral daytime café window light, honest paper texture, small natural creases, plausible label scale, balanced straightforward photography from a mild elevated angle, carefully designed but believable like actual packaging photographed after a small business brand project. No orange colour cast, dramatic rays, fake gold foil, floating pouches, fabricated certifications or origin claims, spelling mistakes, fake reviews, awards, brand claims, watermark, or existing chain coffee logos. Simple slightly condensed wordmark with a small square C mark.
